subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan — ACME Corp (post-call recap & next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmecorp.com>, Mike Duval <mike.duval@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan — ACME Corp (post-call recap & next steps)

Tom / Mike — thanks again for the time earlier. Per our call, attached is an initial Mutual Action Plan (acme_map_draft_v1.xlsx) with the technical evaluation milestone fleshed out. Below is a concise recap + proposed owners / dates so we can lock the timeline.

Summary (goal):
- Objective: Validate a candidate model and serving profile that meets ACME's quality, latency, and unit-cost targets for the customer-support generation workflow.
- Target close for the technical-eval milestone: 2026-12-15 (final recommendation to ACME).

Technical evaluation milestone (proposed) — success criteria, owners, dates, dependencies:
1) Access & Dataset (ACME) — Due: 2026-11-17
   - Deliverables: 25k representative prompts + 5k labeled gold responses (if available) + sample production traffic capture (anonymized).
   - Owner: Mike Duval (ACME) — dependency: S3 bucket access / temporary credentials.

2) Baseline sweep (Redwood) — Due: 2026-11-24
   - Run baseline against ACME's current production model (if allowed) and 3 candidate models to establish quality baselines and cost/latency heuristics.
   - Candidate shortlist (initial): Llama-3 14B (quantized), Mistral-Instruct-7B, Falcon-40B-Instruct (sharded/quantized).
   - Metrics: automated quality (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable), embedding-based similarity to gold (cosine), and representative human-rated quality samples (5-point scale).
   - Owner: Redwood (Marissa / Neha) — dependency: dataset + evaluation spec.

3) Latency & cost benchmarking (Redwood) — Due: 2026-12-01
   - End-to-end p95 latency target (256-token prompt, 128-token generation): <= 200ms p95 for the recommended dedicated serving profile; objective: <150ms where feasible.
   - Cost target: <= $0.10 per 1k output tokens for the recommended config (goal to be refined after baseline).
   - Tests: single-request p95, 50 RPS sustained load profile, and mixed traffic tail-case. Report will include token-level cost, GPU util, and breakdown by model variant/quantization.
   - Owner: Redwood (Rishi / infra team).

4) Quality review & sign-off (ACME) — Due: 2026-12-08
   - Deliverable: summary of human evals, failure modes, recommended inference profile.
   - Owner: ACME (Tom / Mike) to coordinate product SMEs.

5) Final recommendation & next steps (Joint) — Target: 2026-12-15
   - Decision: go/no-go for production rollout or shortlist for Dedicated/Private deployment and pricing.

Open items / dependencies:
- VPC peering or secure upload path from ACME to Redwood for sample capture and result delivery.
- Legal/PII: confirm anonymization requirements and any additional redaction needed before we process logs.
- Access: temporary S3 credentials or a pre-signed bucket object listing.
- If ACME needs hardware-local testing (Private), we’ll need account for infra scheduling — note: Redwood Dedicated test pool availability TBD.

Next steps (asks):
- Mike: confirm dataset availability and delivery method by 2026-11-17.
- Tom: confirm whether we can run initial baseline against current prod model or only anonymized snapshots.
- ACME + Redwood: confirm owners above or suggest changes; if agreed, I’ll update the Google MAP sheet and schedule the alignment call.

Attaching: acme_map_draft_v1.xlsx (MAP), tech-eval-benchmarks.md (bench spec).

Thanks — happy to chat through details on a quick call.

--
Marissa Cole

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan — ACME Corp (post-call recap & next steps)

Marissa — really clear, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Dataset: we can provide ~25k representative prompts by 11/17 and another 25k (anonymized) by 11/18 — that should be enough for the initial sweep. Mike will own delivery.
2) Gold labels: we have about 3k labeled responses; we can push more but may not reach 5k before 11/17. We’ll share what we have.
3) Access: we prefer to avoid cross-account peering for initial baseline. Can you accept upload to a pre-signed S3 path or a secure WeTransfer link?
4) Human eval: what format do you need? We typically do a side-by-side A/B with a 5-point helpfulness scale and a short rationale field. Is that sufficient?
5) Cost for load tests: can you provide a ballpark estimate for running the three candidate models under the 50 RPS profile (one-off test)? We need this internally to budget.

Also looping Mike (product engineering lead) who will coordinate data and any redaction:

- We have a Dedicated test pool window available starting 2026-11-28 that we can reserve for the 50 RPS runs. If ACME prefers, initial baselines can run on Hosted API to get fast turnaround, then move to Dedicated for cost/latency validation.
- Ballpark test cost for a single 50 RPS 30-minute run across 3 models: estimate $3k-$6k depending on model size/quantization. We’ll refine once we know candidate sizes.
- Action: Mike/ACME, if you can provide upload mechanism by 11/17 I’ll open a ticket to reserve the Dedicated window and pre-stage quantized artifacts.
